Upon not receiving the bonus in a timely manner, I contacted Amex first through online chat and then by phone the next day. Several Amex representatives including a manager indicated that charitable donations are considered " Cash Equivalents '' and as per the terms and conditions do not count towards the spending threshold. I explained that no reasonable person would consider a charitable donation to be a cash equivalent, and that I believed American Express was not upholding the terms of their contract. On XX/XX/scrub> 2025, a second {$400.00} credit was issued to my account. No notice, explanation, or correction accompanied that second credit. It remained on my account for over 60 days with no communication from American Express that it was issued in error. 

Then, on XX/XX/year>2025 exactly 61 days later the {$400.00} credit was reversed. I was not informed in advance. I received an email on XX/XX/XXXX, after the charge had already posted. American Express claims this was due to a technical error and that it affected XXXX accounts.

However, before I could respond to American Expresss reply, the CFPB portal marked the complaint closed, denying me the ability to rebut their justification. I am now resubmitting this complaint in full, including my legal rebuttal.

LEGAL REBUTTAL : American Expresss reversal of the {$400.00} credit over 60 days after it was issued, with no advance notice, violates both reasonable customer expectations and key consumer protection principles.

Under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ), 15 U.S.C. 1666b, a card issuer must inform consumers of billing errors in a timely manner and can not unilaterally adjust accounts outside the 60-day dispute window unless the consumer has been properly notified. 

The reversal posted on XX/XX/year>2025, more than 60 days after the XX/XX/XXXX credit was issued. That alone raises serious compliance concerns. There was : No contemporaneous notification in XXXX that the second credit was a mistake No warning or communication prior to the reversal in XXXX No merchant dispute or consumer-initiated correction This was a company-initiated credit and later a company-initiated reversal, executed after a lengthy delay and without transparency. American Expresss response to the CFPB claims no law was violated because the credit was part of a benefit program, not a merchant transaction. But the FCBA governs more than just merchant billing disputes it also covers improper charges and adjustments made to a consumers account without timely disclosure. 

Finally, Amex admitted that XXXX customers were affected yet has not shown proof that any notice was provided to me before the debit occurred. Their reference to an email on XX/XX/XXXX confirms that I was informed after my account was already charged. Thats not transparency its retroactive justification.

narrative:
My name is XXXX XXXX. Ive been in contact with the American Express customer service team regarding the welcome bonus on my Hilton XXXX XXXX with American Express. While the Diamond status, annual free night reward, and the point bonuses were the most exciting aspects of the card, the welcome bonus was also enticing. Having read about the card online, I was aware that if American Express planned to deny a sign up bonus, a popup would appear when applying for the card. 

When this pop-up didnt appear, I was elated, assuming I would qualify for the bonus and could use Hilton points for XXXX vacation stays. I have used the card religiously since acquiring it, knowing Id hit the spend easily and racking up points with the rewards features. However, when the 3 months ended after Id hit the bonus, I started to wonder when my XXXX points would finally post. After a while, I contacted American Express to be told that my account was not approved for the signup bonus. This was a huge surprise to me. 

After going through multiple rounds of contact with American Express, I was told that I would not receive a bonus for several reasons : ( 1 ) I had already used too many Amex bonus offers ( 2 ) I had transferred points away from American Express ( 3 ) I had cancelled too many cards ( 4 ) I hadnt used my previous American Express cards enough.

Regarding point # 1, I only have one previous Amex card - the cash magnet which I used as my primary card for several years. I dont remember if there was a sign-up bonus, but if there was, it was small. 

To point # 2, I have never transferred points from Amex to other carriers. On my cash magnet, I have only taken the Cashback after hitting {$25.00} and on the XXXX card I have always used the points with Hilton. 

On # 3, I have only ever cancelled one credit card, a XXXX card with XXXX XXXX which I cancelled because my wife is a photographer and she travels way more than I do as an attorney so we decided to have her sign up for the card instead of me to take advantage of the travel perks that were only available to cardholders. 

To # 4, admittedly I have dropped the usage of my cash magnet card in recent years because of other cards I opened that have better cash back. However, the XXXX card is the card I most wanted simply because of the cash back and I have dedicated almost 100 % of my spend to it since opening the account. 

However, this experience is changing my mind about that position. The customer service people claimed that I was warned that I wouldnt receive the sign-up bonus both when I was approved for the card and when I received my welcome package. I am 100 % certain I did not receive the pop-up telling me I wouldnt get the sign-up bonus. I have re-opened my welcome package and do not find anything telling me I wasnt given the sign-up bonus. This created a detrimental reliance in which I dedicated myself to the card and made vacation plans assuming I would have XXXX Hilton points. 

Surely the past 6 months of card usage have demonstrated to Amex that my Hilton XXXX card is a profitable account for the company. I want this card regardless of the sign-up bonus, but this experience has left a bad taste in my mouth. I have high income ( {$250000.00} ) and spend A LOT on my credit card. 

For that reason, I requested the following from American Express ( 1 ) Verified documentation that I was advised that I wouldnt receive the sign-up bonus at approval or in the mail. 
( 2 ) Either the full sign-up bonus of XXXX Hilton points or some partial bonus.

narrative:
I am submitting this complaint to formally dispute a fraudulent American Express account that was opened in my name as a result of identity theft. I do not own this account, I did not apply for it, and I never authorized its opening or use. This account was opened without my knowledge or consent, and any balance or activity associated with it is fraudulent. 

The American Express account at issue was opened in or around XX/XX/year> and currently reflects a balance of approximately {$2000.00}. I did not submit any application for credit with American Express during that time, nor did I provide authorization to any third party to do so on my behalf. I have never signed a contract, agreement, or applicationelectronically or otherwiseauthorizing American Express to extend credit to me for this account. I have never received, activated, or used any American Express card or account associated with this tradeline. 

I first became aware of this account after reviewing my credit information and discovering unfamiliar and unauthorized accounts appearing on my credit report. Upon discovering this American Express account, I immediately recognized that it was fraudulent, as I had no prior relationship with American Express related to this account and had not engaged in any transaction that would justify its existence. The presence of this account is entirely inconsistent with my financial history, spending habits, and authorization. 

Because this account was clearly opened through identity theft, I took prompt and reasonable steps to protect myself and mitigate further harm. I filed an official Identity Theft Report with the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ), affirming under penalty of perjury that this account is not mine and was opened fraudulently. This FTC Identity Theft Report documents that my personal identifying information was misused without my authorization and establishes my rights under federal law, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). 

Despite filing an FTC Identity Theft Report and disputing the account, this American Express account continues to be associated with my name and credit profile. This has caused and continues to cause significant harm, including damage to my creditworthiness, emotional distress, time loss, and the burden of repeatedly disputing information that is not accurate. I have been placed in the unfair position of defending myself against a debt that I did not incur and from which I derived no benefit. 

American Express, as a furnisher of credit information and as the alleged creditor, has a legal obligation to ensure that the information it reports is accurate, complete, and verifiable. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, American Express is required to conduct a reasonable investigation when a consumer disputes an account and provides evidence of identity theft, including an FTC Identity Theft Report. Simply confirming information internally or relying on automated systems is not sufficient when the consumer has clearly stated that the account was opened fraudulently and has provided documentation supporting that claim. 

At no point has American Express provided me with any original documentation proving that I applied for or authorized this account. I have not been provided with a signed application, a contract bearing my signature, a valid electronic consent record, an IP address traceable to me, or any other form of original evidence that would demonstrate that I knowingly and willingly opened this account. Without such documentation, there is no legitimate basis for American Express to continue associating this account with me. 

Furthermore, I did not receive any of the funds, credit benefits, or services associated with this account. Any charges, balances, or transactions reported on this account were made by an unknown third party who fraudulently used my personal information. I did not receive billing statements, cards, or notices at the time the account was opened, further supporting the conclusion that the account was opened and controlled by someone else. 

The continued reporting and maintenance of this fraudulent account, despite my identity theft report and disputes, raises serious concerns regarding compliance with federal consumer protection laws. The Fair Credit Reporting Act provides clear protections for victims of identity theft, including the right to have fraudulent information blocked and removed from credit reports once proper documentation is provided. By continuing to report this account or failing to remove it, American Express XXXX be failing to meet its obligations under the law. 

This situation has forced me to spend an unreasonable amount of time correcting information that should never have been attributed to me in the first place. I have had to monitor my credit, submit disputes, file identity theft reports, and repeatedly explain that I am a victim of fraud. These efforts would not be necessary if American Express had exercised appropriate verification and fraud prevention measures at the time the account was opened or during the dispute process. 

I am not refusing to pay a legitimate debt ; rather, I am asserting that no valid debt exists between myself and American Express for this account. I have no contractual obligation to American Express for this account because I never entered into any agreement with them. Any attempt to hold me responsible for this account is improper and unsupported by evidence. 

I am requesting that American Express acknowledge that this account was opened as a result of identity theft, cease all collection or reporting activities related to it, and permanently remove the account from my credit file. I am also requesting confirmation that this account will not be sold, transferred, reassigned, or reinserted into my credit report in the future. 

Additionally, I request that American Express conduct a full and lawful investigation into this matter, including a review of the application data, IP addresses, device information, and any third-party involvement that XXXX have contributed to the fraudulent opening of this account. This investigation should focus on identifying the fraud and correcting the harm done to me as the victim, rather than attempting to shift responsibility onto me. 

In summary, the American Express account opened in XX/XX/year> with a balance of approximately {$2000.00} is fraudulent, was opened without my authorization, and is the direct result of identity theft. I have filed an FTC Identity Theft Report documenting this fraud. I do not own this account, I did not benefit from it, and I have no legal responsibility for it. I am requesting immediate removal of this account and full compliance with applicable consumer protection laws.

To Whom It May Concern, This letter is to request reconsideration of the recent cancellation of American Express account ending in XXXX, as indicated in the letter dated XX/XX/2024. The letter stated that the account was closed due to abusive language directed towards representatives, but there appears to be a misunderstanding that needs to be clarified. 

Representatives were contacted to dispute fraudulent charges made by a contractor named XXXX XXXX, who operates under XXXX XXXX XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, a charge of {$2600.00} was made to the account by this contractor, which was approved and later successfully disputed. Subsequently, a second charge of {$2600.00} was taken without permission on XX/XX/XXXX and was declined by Amex for exceeding my available balance. Following this, XXXX more fraudulent charges of {$1000.00}, {$500.00}, and {$250.00} were transacted successfully. Despite the initial decline, no action was taken to protect the account, allowing the fraudulent charges to proceed until the account was maxed out and there was no more available credit. Additionally, over a dozen attempts to charge various amounts were blocked by Amex. These charges were reported in good faith, as XXXX XXXX was found to be impersonating a contractor and has a criminal record. Amex conducted a thorough investigation and reversed all the fraudulent charges. A criminal complaint has been filed against XXXX XXXX with XXXX XXXX from the Arizona Registrar of Contractors ( Case XXXX ). 

Even though I was a victim of financial fraud, the account has always been maintained in good standing and Amex bills have been paid on time. Due to XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX  ) and XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ), the stress and complexity of this situation had a disproportionate impact. According to the National Institutes of Health ( NIH ), symptoms of XXXX can include irritability, agitation, and mood swings, particularly when exacerbated by stress. In the haste to report the crime, language that could be perceived as offensive may have been unintentionally used. If any communications were construed as abusive, a sincere apology is extended. It was never the intention to disrespect or harm anyone. Actions were driven by the urgency and frustration of being a victim of a significant financial crime. XXXX and XXXX are currently being managed with the help of medical professionals. 

An employee named XXXX indicated that the alleged abuse took place on a call dated XX/XX/2024, and filed a claim ( XXXX ) to allow the back team to review the call. However, no calls were made to Amex on that date. During this time, prank phone calls were being received from XXXX XXXX and the police had to be contacted regarding his behavior. It seems possible that XXXX XXXX may have contacted the bank on that date. When called back, a different time frame was given, and the representative refused to provide the date of the alleged activity. Instead of educating on what the alleged abusive behavior was to curtail it in the future or allowing reference to the specific conversation, it was stated that a subpoena would be required for that information. 

The lack of clear communication and transparency regarding the specific policy allegedly violated is concerning. While it is understood that American Express reserves the right to " cancel or suspend any feature on your Account '' at its discretion, such actions should be taken fairly and transparently. The Cardmember Agreement provided does not list abusive language as a reason for cancellation, making it difficult to understand the basis for this action. Under the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), specifically Regulation Z ( XXXX and XXXX ), creditors are required to clearly and conspicuously disclose terms and conditions, including any circumstances under which an account may be closed. The enforcement of an undisclosed " moral clause '' related to abusive language appears to be a violation of TILA 's requirement for transparency and clear disclosure. 

Additionally, effective XX/XX/2024, American Express is amending the Cardmember Agreement to include the ability to cancel or suspend accounts " at any time and for any reason. '' This clause was not part of the agreement at the time the account was canceled, suggesting that the current action may not be supported by the terms of the agreement in effect when the decision was made. Furthermore, as of today, XX/XX/2024, the Card Membership Agreement still lists the available limit as {$8000.00}, which contradicts the letter dated XX/XX/2024, stating the account was canceled. 

Multiple representatives stated that there was no way to appeal the decision and that it was final. This contradicts the terms outlined in the Cardmember Agreement, which specifies the method to appeal any decision. If the Cardmember Agreement includes an appeal process, American Express is required to inform cardholders of this process in its communication regarding adverse decisions. The absence of such information in the notice received could be considered a violation of TILAs requirements for clear and conspicuous disclosure and may also constitute a breach of contract and a violation of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing. As such, the failure to follow its own stated procedures and provide a clear appeal process means that the decision to cancel the account is procedurally incorrect and invalid, irrespective of the alleged language. 

Moreover, the Americans with Disabilities Act ( ADA ) and Section XXXX of the Rehabilitation Act require that people with XXXX be provided with reasonable accommodations and not be discriminated against. These laws mandate clear and effective communication with individuals with XXXX, ensuring that procedures are fair and transparent. As a person with XXXX and XXXX, membership in a protected class should be considered, and interactions with Amex should consider the impact of these conditions. 

The notice regarding the federal Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) states that creditors are prohibited from discriminating against credit applicants on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age, or because the applicant has in good faith exercised any right under the Consumer Credit Protection Act. According to 15 U.S.C. 1691 ( a ), discrimination based on XXXX, including XXXX and XXXX, can be considered discriminatory. Penalizing for the symptoms of XXXX while exercising rights under the Consumer Credit Protection Act could be seen as discriminatory. 

Furthermore, under the Consumer Financial Protection Act ( CFPA ), financial institutions are prohibited from engaging in unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ). The lack of clear communication, transparency, and the enforcement of undisclosed policies could be considered unfair and abusive under the CFPA. This situation has caused significant distress and confusion, further exacerbating medical conditions. 

Given these circumstances, the closure of the account appears retaliatory for filing legitimate disputes of fraud and criminal behavior. It is believed that the closure of the account without considering the context of XXXX and without providing an opportunity for appeal or reasonable accommodation may be inconsistent with these federal obligations. A respectful request is made for Amex to reconsider the decision to cancel the account, taking into account the medical conditions and the extraordinary stress caused by the fraudulent activities. 

In the event that the request for reconsideration is not addressed satisfactorily, a formal claim will be filed through the arbitration process as outlined in the Cardmember Agreement. This step is believed necessary to ensure fair treatment and adherence to the protections afforded by federal laws. 

The relationship with Amex is valued, and the support and services provided have always been appreciated. Please understand that behavior during this period was influenced by XXXX  conditions, and it is assured that a respectful and cooperative relationship with Amex will be maintained in the future. 

Thank you for your understanding and consideration.

narrative:
Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am writing this letter as a complaint on my {$10000.00} pending chargeback dispute for my business card with American Express.

1. Facts I purchased a travel package bundle from a company called XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in early XX/XX/XXXX and paid for that product with two of my American Express cards : ( 1 ) card X and ( 2 ) card Y. Shortly after my purchase, I paid approximately {$5000.00} towards the balance on my card Y leaving approximately {$5000.00} in an outstanding balance.

Within a week of my purchase, I did not receive the product that I purchased and attempted to reach out to the vendor. After weeks of no response from the vendor, I called American Express and requested a chargeback on both of my cards. American Express representatives assured me that if I did not receive my product, I would be issued a chargeback for my purchase.

Within weeks after my chargeback request, a successful chargeback was placed towards my card X for the travel bundle purchase clearing the approximately {$20000.00} debt on that card. Card Y card, however, did not receive a chargeback. After hearing nothing for weeks, I called American Express and was told that the dispute was ruled in the favor of the vendor DESPITE BEING FOR THE EXACT SAME PRODUCT AND VENDOR.

Confused as to how one card, but not the other, would receive the chargeback, I then spoke with an American Express customer representative manager. I requested an explanation for why American Express ruled in favor of the merchant and was told that my contact information would be taken down for someone to explain to me the investigation. Per the managers recommendations, I requested opened a second chargeback dispute. I further offered myself to be a source of information for the dispute and requested that any chargeback investigators call me at my personal cell. Despite this, I heard nothing from American Express for three months. During this time, I was never contacted for information, learned about the status of my chargeback, or was given an explanation of the first chargeback result.

To my surprise and disbelief, I suddenly began receiving aggressive debt collector calls towards the end of XX/XX/XXXX demanding I pay the {$5000.00} outstanding balance on card Y. Upon calling American Express, I was abruptly told that the chargeback was ruled in the favor of the merchant again, and despite my multiple demands, was given no reason how or why the investigation ruled in favor of the merchant. To make matters even worse, multiple American Express refused to speak to me telling me there was nothing they could do further for me because my account was now outsourced to an external debt collector.

Frustrated and exasperated, I secured an evidentiary letter from the vendor stating that I never received the product that I purchased and that the vendor had gone bankrupt immediately after I purchased the product. Based on the letter from the vendor, American Express representatives reversed course and opened a third chargeback investigation. That chargeback investigation is now the topic of why I am writing this letter today nearly one year after the purchase.

2. Multiple Violations of 12 CFR 226.13, Truth in Lending Act American Expresss handling of my chargeback has resulted in multiple blatant violations of my rights under the Truth and Lending Act. They are as follows : Under 12 CFR 226.13 Billing Error Resolution, Section ( f ), American Express is required to conduct a reasonable investigation into my chargeback demand. The Consumer Finance and Protection Bureaus ( hereafter CFPB ) official interpretation of a reasonable investigation for a chargeback is : NONDELIVERY OF PROPERTY OR SERVICES : In conducting an investigation of a billing error notice alleging the nondelivery of property or services under 1026.13 ( a ) ( 3 ), the creditor shall not deny the assertion unless it conducts a reasonable investigation that the property or services were actually delivered, mailed or sent as agreed.

American Express has failed to conduct a reasonable investigation as required. The three investigations have consisted of calling the defunct vendor, not receiving a response, and ruling in favor of the vendor based on not receiving a response. These investigations have produced nothing aside from a non-response from the defunct vendor. They can not meet the statutory burden of proof that rests with American Express to show that I ( the debtor ) received the product that I purchased. This violation is made even more blatant considering ( 1 ) that American Express has already processed a chargeback on my other American Express card for the exact same product and vendor and ( 2 ) that I have furnished an evidentiary letter from the defunct vendor stating that I never received the product that I purchased.

Under 12 CFR 226.13 Billing Error Resolution, Section ( f ), if American Express determines that I am not due a chargeback, American Express must : ( 1 ) Mail or deliver to the consumer an explanation that sets forth the reasons for the creditor 's belief that the billing error alleged by the consumer is incorrect in whole or in part ; ( 2 ) Furnish copies of documentary evidence of the consumer 's indebtedness, if the consumer so requests.

American Express, despite my numerous written and oral pleas, has failed to produce any oral, written, or electronic explanation setting forth its belief that the billing error alleged by me is incorrect in whole or in part. After requesting to speak to an investigator to understand why my first two chargebacks were denied, I ( the debtor ) was told, on multiple occasions, that I can not talk to American Express investigators. In addition, a written demand for proof of documentary evidence of my consumer indebtedness was sent to American Express XXXX XXXX XXXX, Utah office and received via certified mail on XX/XX/XXXX. Documentary evidence of indebtedness, or for that matter a basic response, was never sent to me.

To make matters even worse, American Express has refused to do this for both chargeback investigations concluded on this card.

Under 12 CFR 226.13 Billing Error Resolution, Section ( c ) ( 2 ), American Express must conclude my dispute within 90 days : The creditor shall comply with the appropriate resolution procedures of paragraphs ( e ) and ( f ) of this section, as applicable, within 2 complete billing cycles ( but in no event later than 90 days ) after receiving a billing error notice.

American Express opened its first chargeback into my card on XX/XX/XXXX. As of XX/XX/XXXX, 190 days has passed a full 100 days and counting past the statutory limit.

3. Conclusion I hope these quickly identified violations of the Truth in Lending Act will prompt American Express to rectify from how it has bungled this chargeback. I am very eagerly looking forward to the CFPB 's response to my complaint.

narrative:
In 2018 I opened a credit line with American Express because of the {$200.00} cash back promise offered if I spent {$1000.00} dollars in the first three months of opening the account. The card also had a 0 % interest introductory offer for 12 months. 

Soon after receiving the card in the mail, I went on a 4 week road trip where I was not regularly checking my emails. I was using the card regularly on the trip and felt confident I would reach the {$1000.00} spending goal by purchasing meals and gas on my trip. 

I connected my bank account for automatic ACH payments and always have had more than enough cash available to cover the entire balance on the card. 

Towards the end of my trip, I logged into my email to see a notice that said my card was being cancelled for non-payment. 

This must be an error, I thought. My bank account was connected and I accepted all of the terms for automatic payments. I had never received any call, never had a voicemail, and never spoke with a human about that status of my account - I only received a single email telling me of a failed payment, and then soon after an email that my account was being closed. 

I called as soon as possible and was told that there was a failed payment on my account. I told the representative there must be an error and re-entered my bank account details ( double checking every number ) so the payment would go through without issue, and asked the representative that they submit a request to not cancel my card. A few days later I got another notice ( by email ) that the payment failed, and that my request to prevent the cancellation was denied. 

I called again and I said there must be an error because I double checked my payment information to be correct. Eventually the American Express representative and I conference called with my bank and were able to get a payment of {$400.00} to go through ( well above the minimum payment, in good faith ). 

At that time I also requested that my card not be cancelled as I had made every effort to make my payments on time, and had been completely able to do so. I was told to wait and someone would reach out to me about the decision, but that I could keep using my card and that the late fees would be removed as a courtesy. 

A couple days later, still no word from anyone at American Express, I reached out again to see the status. I was told that my request was denied and my card would be cancelled. I told them they could cancel the card if they wanted, but I still would like to spend the remaining amount required to receive my cash back bonus. 

At this point in time I was approximately {$20.00} away from reaching my {$1000.00} spending goal to get my {$200.00} cash back reward. 

To my dismay, the card was cancelled immediately thereafter, preventing me from spending another {$20.00} on gas or any other purchase. I saw on my account that not only did I still have the late fee charges on my account, but also I had been charged interest on the debt. 

At this point I arrived back in Hawaii and still wanted to resolve this issue. Because Hawaii is a one-party consent state, I began recording all of my communications with American Express. 

I spoke with multiple people including customer service managers and was eventually told that I would have any interest and late fees removed from my account ( It was a 0 % interested rate card ), and that they would look into whether American Express could honor their cashback offer which was the reason I signed up for the card in the first place. I was told that I would be contacted, and to wait. 

Over the next several weeks I would not receive any communication from American Express, causing me to reach out on my own, and be told the same thing as the previous conversation, this time by another manager. I was told that the representative would initiate an investigation into my cashback bonus and in the meantime would remove the interest and fees. Each time I spoke with someone I was told that I would receive a call. Each time, I never received any type of communication back. 

Eventually my account was closed and sent to XXXX XXXX. I spoke with a manager at American Express and asked them to recall the account from the collection agency so we could resolve it. He told me he would do what he could and to wait for a response. Once again, I heard nothing. I reached out to XXXX XXXX and asked that they send the account back to American Express so we could resolve our dispute. 

I called American Express and told them again about the situation, they said that they would try to accept the account back, would remove the interest and late charges as I was repeatedly told would happen, and that I could expect a call from the legal department about my situation. 

Surprise! I was never contacted. 

That was the last I have been in contact with American Express or XXXX XXXX, Now, however, I am getting calls from a different collection agency called XXXX. 

I'm honestly not sure who owns this account any more, but I am quite upset about the way that I was treated by American Express - I feel lied to, cheated and defrauded. 

I would like to resolve this issue without needing to escalate it any further. 

I am only looking to find a fair outcome to this situation, and my hope is that we can resolve things amicably.

1. **Excessive Transfers and Queue Loops : ** - Our initial attempts to contact American Express customer service were met with repeated transfers between representatives. narrative: I am familiar with The Card Act of 2009, in particular, Paragraph 164. " Prompt and fair crediting of payments, Section ( b ) APPLICATION OF PAYMENTS, '' which states that any amounts above the minimum payment must first be applied to the card balance bearing the highest rate of interest. American Express is attempting to circumvent this law by using the expression " Plan Fee '' rather than Interest Charges or Finance Charges so they can apply payment amounts above the minimum due towards balances with lower fees rather than the highest fee. Representatives at AMEX stated that " it's not interest, it's a plan fee, so the Card Act does not apply. '' Their disclosure, however, refers to a " Plan Fee '' as a " Fixed Finance Charge '' as found on page 1 of 4 of " Cardmember Agreement, Part 1 of 2, '' and the " Plan Fee '' calculation method ties it to the APR for the account. Presently I have six balances that have " Planned '' repayment schedules which carry a zero interest rate, and two plans that carry interest rates of more that 25 %. Today I tried to pay off one of these high interest rate plans early, and I was told my payment would first be applied to the plan balance with the lowest plan fee ( interest rate ) first. This is in direct violation of spirit and language of the Card Act of 2009. I have a credit card with American Express that has a set credit limit and it is revolving. There are balances which I am not paying and full, and as such I must pay extra money to AMEX above and beyond the principal amount that I charged on my card. That amount of money is based upon the APR set on my account. Whether AMEX chooses to call it " interest charges, '' " finance charges, " plan fees, '' or simply " widgets '' -- the NAME should be set aside and the character of and reason I am paying more money every month above the principal balance should be considered to conclude that the relationship is subject to the Card Act of 2009, binding the card issuer to apply payments according to the law : balances with higher interest rates first.

Subject : Formal Complaint of Discriminatory Practices in Credit Card Denial by American Express RE : American Express XXXX Credit Card XXXX American Express XXXX : American Express Company, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, NY XXXX Transaction Date : XX/XX/year> Amount Applied For : Open ended To the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), I, XXXX XXXX, hereby file this formal complaint against American Express for unlawfully denying my application for an American Express XXXX Credit Card. The decision to deny my credit application was based on my credit score and prior financial history, despite my demonstrated ability and capacity to contract, comply with lawful tender under the Federal Reserve Act, and my adherence to all necessary legal requirements. This decision constitutes discriminatory treatment and violates several state and federal statutes aimed at protecting consumer rights.

1. Violation of Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) American Express denied my credit card application based on my credit score and alleged " negative entries. '' Under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1691 ), creditors are prohibited from denying credit on discriminatory grounds, including age and irrelevant financial history that does not directly affect the transaction in question. ECOA mandates that all credit applicants are entitled to fair and equal treatment when applying for financial services. However, by relying exclusively on a biased XXXX XXXX metric, American Express has denied me equal access to financial services. This decision not only disregards my demonstrated ability to contract, but it also constitutes age-based discrimination in violation of federal law. 
XXXX. Discriminatory Practices in Credit Issuance The reliance on arbitrary credit scores for credit card approval is an inherently discriminatory practice that disproportionately affects individuals with lower credit scores, many of whom face such challenges due to temporary or unrelated financial issues. This violates the principle of equal access to credit. Florida Statute 559.72 ( 3 ) under the Consumer Collection Practices Act ( CCPA ) expressly prohibits the use of deceptive or unfair trade practices in the denial of financial services. By denying me a fair opportunity to obtain credit, American Express has engaged in such discriminatory practices in direct violation of this statute. 
XXXX. Violation of Federal Reserve Act XXXX. XXXX ( 1 ) and ( 2 ) In addition, I complied fully with XXXX XXXXXXXX ( XXXX ) and ( XXXX ) of the Federal Reserve Act, which regulates the issuance of credit and credit card applications. My lawful tender of application and adherence to the Federal Reserves policies on creditworthiness were entirely disregarded by American Express. The bank 's failure to process my application in accordance with federal credit laws is a direct violation of these provisions, and demonstrates discrimination based on my financial history in violation of my rights to fair access to credit. 
XXXX. Failure to Acknowledge the Consumers Right to Negotiate Terms As a consumer, I have the legal right to negotiate the terms of any credit or loan transaction that does not align with my needs or financial position. This is a fundamental right under contract law, which governs all financial transactions. American Express 's refusal to engage in a fair and open negotiation of terms reflects a broader disregard for my right to be treated as a contracting party with the capacity to engage in financial agreements. 
By denying my application outright and failing to explore alternative terms or solutions, American Express has obstructed my right to negotiate, in violation of the Truth in Lending Act ( XXXX ), which requires fairness, transparency, and the opportunity for consumers to understand and negotiate the terms of their credit agreements. 
XXXX. Failure to Recognize My Capacity to Contract My capacity to contract is a key element in this matter, as American Express has disregarded my lawful standing to enter into a valid credit agreement. Under basic contract law principles, the capacity to contract is defined as the legal ability to enter into binding agreements. I have demonstrated my ability and willingness to engage in such agreements by fully complying with the legal standards governing credit applications, including the submission of lawful tender under the Federal Reserve Act. Therefore, the denial of my application, despite my clear ability to contract, constitutes an unlawful obstruction and discriminatory practice.

6. Right to Redress and Non-Discriminatory Credit Services I am seeking redress for the unlawful denial of my credit card application and for the discriminatory practices that led to this decision. I request that American Express immediately reconsider my application and engage in a fair negotiation of credit terms, evaluating my full financial capacity and removing any discriminatory reliance on arbitrary credit scoring systems. 
Conclusion and Request for Redress I respectfully request the following actions from the CFPB : Investigation of American Expresss discriminatory practices in denying my credit card application based on biased credit scores and failure to recognize my right to contract and negotiate fair terms. 
Reconsideration of my credit card application by American Express under terms that align with both state and federal consumer protection laws, including the opportunity to negotiate alternative terms. 
A full review of American Expresss compliance with the Federal Reserve Act, Equal Credit Opportunity Act, and Truth in Lending Act to ensure they are adhering to their obligations to provide non-discriminatory and fair access to credit services.
